name: CAME 12-bit gate remote
description: CAME gate and garage remotes in their twelve bit form, and the many clones that copy them. The bit is carried by a gap followed by a pulse of constant total length: a short gap with a long pulse is a one, a long gap with a short pulse is a zero. That is the wrong way round for this schema, whose data symbols must begin with a pulse, so the definition sets "invert" — the flag that exists for exactly these chips — and describes the inverted stream, where the frame separator becomes a long pulse and each bit becomes pulse-then-gap. Reading it the other way, as pulse-then-gap on the raw stream, decodes a frame of all ones correctly and then falls apart on the first zero — a reminder that an internally consistent decode is not the same as a correct one. The structure matches Nice FLO: a long separator and 1:2 pulse width modulation, differing only in the timing element, which is why both are drafts and identification leans on the measured element rather than the nominal one.

devices.note: decodes as CAME at 333 us; attribution is ours, not confirmed
